mass_renormalization_convention.rationale: The accepted CT18 family uses a charm pole-mass convention and serializes 1.3 and 4.75 GeV; selecting APFEL pole masses avoids converting a repository-bound family to an unreviewed running-mass contract.

charm_mass_gev.rationale: CT18NLO DataVersion 1 serializes MCharm=1.3000 and the CT18 publication identifies mc=1.3 GeV as a pole mass.

bottom_mass_gev.rationale: CT18NLO DataVersion 1 and the CT18 publication bind mb=4.75 GeV.

threshold_relationship.value: mu_c=mc_pole; mu_b=mb_pole; top inactive below the five-flavor project ceiling
threshold_relationship.rationale: APFEL SetPoleMasses uses pole masses as VFN thresholds; this also matches the accepted family metadata.

alpha_s_contract.active_flavor_relation: nf changes at 1.3 and 4.75 GeV and is capped at nf=5; top is outside scope
alpha_s_contract.identity_source: CT18NLO DataVersion 1 metadata plus the accepted repository evolution precedent
alpha_s_contract.apfel_binding: APFEL internally evolves alpha_s from the repository-owned reference tuple through SetAlphaQCDRef(0.118,91.187), perturbative order 1, pole-mass thresholds and nf ceiling 5; no APFEL default supplies a load-bearing value.
alpha_s_contract.independent_reference_binding: Independent references receive the same reference tuple but evolve it in their own implementation; copying APFEL's sampled alpha_s table would not be independent.

anchor_rationale: The nine points are the Cartesian center, four axis endpoints and four corners of the already accepted two-parameter validation box. They are fixed before execution and cannot be replaced adaptively.

physics_validity_domain.pdf_support_relation: The entire effective domain lies inside x in [1e-9,1] and Q in [1.295,1e5] GeV; every query is nevertheless checked before evaluation.
physics_validity_domain.boundary_semantics: Closed validation and normalization domain; boundary values are included and never deleted after observing results.
physics_validity_domain.rationale: The HERA publication supplies the beam-scale kinematic envelope. The lower Q2 boundary is explicitly raised to the HERA perturbative-QCD fit floor of 3.5 GeV2; this is an analysis-validity choice, not a claim that the experimental range defines theory validity.

curves: y=0.005 and y=0.95 at every x node
Q2=3.5 and Q2=50000 GeV2 at every admissible x node
Q2=mb^2*(1-2^-10), mb^2, mb^2*(1+2^-10) at every admissible x node
x=Q2/(Q2+4*mh^2) times (1-2^-10), 1, (1+2^-10) for h=c,b at every admissible Q2 node
validation_grids.charm_evolution_threshold_note: Q2=mc^2 is below the declared Q2 floor; it is not pulled into the physics domain. Charm and bottom production-threshold curves are still probed where admissible.
validation_grids.rationale: The tensor grids cover the interior while exact boundary and one-sided threshold curves test support, evolution-threshold and heavy-production-threshold sensitivity without result-adaptive point insertion.

validation_grids.independent_rule: tensor Clenshaw-Curtis implemented without APFEL integration utilities
validation_grids.domain_mapping: For each x, Q2_low=max(3.5,101200*x*0.005) and Q2_high=min(50000,101200*x*0.95); skip empty intervals and include the x*Q2 log-coordinate Jacobian.
validation_grids.rationale: Nested fixed-order rules make all evaluation locations and costs predeclared and provide an algorithmically distinct redundant integral.

tolerances.comparison_reference: successive fixed refinement levels and the independent quadrature rule
tolerances.numerical_precision_context: binary64 evaluations with deterministic log-coordinate quadrature
tolerances.justification_text: The numerical discretization budget is one tenth of the 0.013 published full-scheme component-comparison envelope, keeping integration/grid error subdominant to the weakest independent physics reference.
tolerances.failure_consequence: NORMALIZATION_FAILURE or INCONCLUSIVE when only convergence is unresolved

tolerances.quantity: absolute residual of integral_A p_theta dx dQ2 and lossless selected-event normalization from one
tolerances.numerical_precision_context: dimensionless normalized integral from both fixed quadrature implementations
tolerances.justification_text: For a unit target, the same subdominant 0.0013 numerical budget is an absolute probability-mass budget.

tolerances.quantity: relative discrepancy between APFEL alpha_s and an independent high-precision two-loop solution
tolerances.comparison_reference: independent two-loop implicit RGE solver with residual <=8*u, u=2^-53
tolerances.numerical_precision_context: binary64 APFEL result against at least binary128 reference
tolerances.justification_text: The threshold is 72*u: 64*u for the bounded binary64 evaluation path plus 8*u for the independent solver residual, rather than a decimal convention.

tolerances.quantity: relative discrepancy of numerical and analytic dy/dQ2
tolerances.justification_text: Eight unit roundoffs cover the two products/divisions and comparison against the analytic expression.

tolerances.quantity: negative complete differential rate attributable only to floating-point assembly
tolerances.threshold: gamma_32*S where gamma_32=32*u/(1-32*u)=3.5527136788005136e-15 and S is the sum of absolute assembled rate terms
tolerances.comparison_reference: same point recomputed with at least binary128 arithmetic
tolerances.numerical_precision_context: binary64 primary and at least binary128 sign adjudication
tolerances.justification_text: gamma_32 is the standard forward-error envelope for at most 32 rounded elementary operations in the declared outer rate assembly. A point is roundoff-compatible only when its magnitude is within this envelope and the higher-precision recomputation is nonnegative.
tolerances.failure_consequence: NEGATIVE_RATE unless both roundoff conditions hold; no value is repaired

convergence_rules.pass: For both quadrature families, |I2-I1|/|I2|<=0.0013 and either I1=I0=I2 or |I2-I1|<=0.5*|I1-I0|; the two I2 values also agree within 0.0013 relative.
convergence_rules.fail: Any estimate is nonfinite or nonpositive, or the two converged methods disagree beyond 0.0013 after level 2.
convergence_rules.inconclusive: All estimates are finite and positive but the fixed three-level reduction test is not met.

convergence_rules.pass: L1 and L2 have the same finite/support/positivity classification and reported extrema change by at most 0.0013 relative when their local scale is nonzero.
convergence_rules.fail: A predeclared point is unsupported/nonfinite or a physical negative rate is found at any level.
convergence_rules.inconclusive: Classifications are admissible but extrema do not stabilize by L2.

convergence_rules.pass: All exact boundary and one-sided sequences remain in declared support, require no extrapolation, and have stable finite/positivity classifications between L1 and L2.
convergence_rules.fail: Any evaluation extrapolates, clips, deletes a point, or produces a nonfinite/physical negative rate.
convergence_rules.inconclusive: No hard failure occurs but a one-sided classification changes at the final level.

convergence_rules.pass: Every level is nonnegative, except recorded roundoff-compatible negatives satisfying TOL_NEGATIVE_ROUNDOFF_ENVELOPE, and no new non-roundoff negative appears at L2.
convergence_rules.fail: Any higher-precision result is negative or any binary64 negative exceeds gamma_32*S.
convergence_rules.inconclusive: The higher-precision sign or local error scale cannot be established within the fixed resource bound.

convergence_rules.pass: Every reference discrepancy is within its source-bound tolerance and changes by no more than one tenth of that tolerance under the final internal refinement.
convergence_rules.fail: A stable discrepancy exceeds its source-bound tolerance or a reference identity/configuration mismatch is found.
convergence_rules.inconclusive: The discrepancy has not stabilized by the final allowed refinement or the pinned reference cannot execute reproducibly.

independent_reference_hierarchy.gate_interpretation: A decomposition is sufficient because the accepted gate asks for an independent plan for formulae, normalization, support and sampling, and the FONLL observable is an explicit additive composition. Every load-bearing layer has an independent or analytic check; no APFEL wrapper is credited as independent. A future result must report layer failures separately and may not promote component agreement to an unqualified full-code equivalence claim.

resource_bounds.point_grid_candidate_formula_per_level: N^2+13*N for N in [17,33,65] before deterministic domain filtering
resource_bounds.wall_clock_rule: No arbitrary scientific wall-clock gate. Exceeding any structural count or output bound stops with INCONCLUSIVE; wall time is recorded only as provenance.
resource_bounds.derivation: 63882=9*((17^2+13*17)+(33^2+13*33)+(65^2+13*65)); 98811=9*((16^2+32^2+64^2)+(17^2+33^2+65^2)); 310=64 FONLL published records+30 massless benchmark coordinates+9*24 analytic project points. The 64 MiB output cap allocates about 32 MiB for <=63882 compact point records and the remainder for integration, references and provenance.

positivity_no_hidden_clipping_contract.quantity: complete APFEL FONLL-A NLO unpolarized e- p d2sigma/dx_Bj/dQ2 including gamma/Z terms
positivity_no_hidden_clipping_contract.roundoff_semantics: A negative binary64 value is only ROUND_OFF_COMPATIBLE_NEGATIVE when |rate|<=gamma_32*S and an at-least-binary128 recomputation is nonnegative. It remains recorded with its raw sign and is never changed.
positivity_no_hidden_clipping_contract.physical_negative_consequence: FAIL at NEGATIVE_RATE or contract-review trigger before normalization or downstream use

normalization_closure_contract.independent_evaluation: separately implemented fixed tensor Clenshaw-Curtis orders 17,33,65
normalization_closure_contract.selected_event_check: For the Phase 2B lossless-detector closure epsilon(z)=1, alpha_theta=1 and q_theta=p_theta; both quadratures must give integral q_theta=1 within TOL_NORMALIZED_LAW. A nontrivial detector kernel remains Phase 2D work.
normalization_closure_contract.failure_precedence: Any nonfinite, nonpositive or unconverged Z_theta blocks normalized-law construction and all later sampling.

remaining_limitations: No single independent implementation covers the complete accepted theta-dependent gamma/Z FONLL-A observable end to end; the plan uses an explicit independently checked decomposition and forbids an unqualified full-code-equivalence claim.
Pointwise positivity, finite positive normalization, convergence and independent numerical agreement remain untested post-authorization questions.
The nine validation anchors are not a prior and do not prove behavior at every interior theta without the separately authorized fixed-grid study.
Inclusive NC e-p data do not provide unrestricted full-flavor separation.
next_step: A separate authorization review may decide whether to authorize execution of this fixed Phase 2B validation plan; this record does not authorize execution.
